analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM brief: the 8:30 a.m. ET data are now in, and they did not rescue the tape. Q3 GDP beat at 3.4% annualized (vs ~3.2% expected) while headline PCE rose 0.5% m/m to 3.6% y/y and core PCE rose 0.3% m/m to 3.1% y/y, both as expected — stronger growth plus still-hot inflation, which keeps the December-hike pricing (~83-84%) intact rather than cooling it. Futures stayed modestly lower after the prints, and the Dow flipped from +0.1% at 5 AM to -0.3% as Caterpillar's ~9% drop now drags the industrials. The morning's second big story is software: ServiceNow -19% on a miss and Fortinet -26% despite a beat on slowing product-revenue growth extend the 'beats are not enough' theme from Lilly/Caterpillar into enterprise software, while DoorDash's $17B Instacart deal (+5-7%) plus a Q3 revenue/EBITDA beat is the one clear risk-on offset outside healthcare. Signal: the market is grading on cash conversion, guidance, and segment detail — Alphabet's cash burn, Caterpillar's held guidance, ServiceNow's miss, Fortinet's product slowdown — not headline beats. Noise: the Marvell/Lumentum talks are still a single Bloomberg report with no company comment, and the Vance/Iran letter remains a reported overture. Into the open, the question is whether the GDP/PCE combo holds futures near current levels or pushes yields higher, ahead of Amazon and Intel after the close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Fresh this morning — Q3 GDP beats, PCE lands as expected: GDP grew 3.4% annualized (vs ~3.2% expected), headline PCE +0.5% m/m to 3.6% y/y, core PCE +0.3% m/m to 3.1% y/y, consumer spending +0.5% (slowing from +0.9%). S&P 500 futures stayed modestly lower after the data; December-hike odds ~83-84%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Stronger growth plus as-expected hot inflation keeps the Fed-hike story alive into the open — no relief for rate-sensitive tech.

headlines.headline: Futures into the open: Nasdaq 100 futures -1.1%, S&P 500 futures -0.3%, Dow futures -0.3% — the Dow flipped from +0.1% at 5 AM as Caterpillar's drop now drags it lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff broadened slightly into the open — no longer just a Nasdaq story, with industrials joining tech lower.

headlines.headline: Alphabet deepens to ~11% lower premarket: Q3 revenue $127.58B vs ~$128.22B expected, search ads $63.35B vs $64.96B expected, negative $9.07B free cash flow, with AI Mode monetizing below traditional search and 2027 capex set to rise significantly.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still the tape's main weight — the cash-burn plus ads-miss combination is what the GDP/PCE prints did nothing to offset.

headlines.headline: Microsoft cools to +1.5% premarket (from +3.5% at 5 AM) on its fiscal Q1 beat (revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, $18.6B free cash flow despite $45.2B capex); buyout report for ~60,000 of 223,000 staff still in the mix.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still the standing offset to Alphabet, but the fade from +3.5% to +1.5% shows even the cash-backed winner is not immune to the morning's risk-off drift.

headlines.headline: Caterpillar still ~9% lower premarket despite the Q3 beat (revenue $20.7B, adjusted EPS $7.20, margin up 310 bps to 20.6%) — guidance only maintained, and construction-industry sales came in slightly below estimates.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh detail this hour — the segment miss explains the drop better than the headline beat, and it is why the Dow flipped negative.

headlines.headline: DoorDash to buy Instacart for ~$17B at $65/share (11% premium to Wednesday's close, 26% to Oct 22 before deal reports), plus Q3 revenue +34% to $4.6B and adjusted EBITDA +41% to $1.06B; DoorDash +5-7% premarket, Instacart/Maplebear +~5%. Close targeted late 2027 or H1 2028, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's clearest fresh deal news — a beat plus a big strategic bet being rewarded, the opposite of the Caterpillar/ServiceNow reaction.

headlines.headline: Software sinks: ServiceNow -19% after missing Q3 profit estimates; Fortinet -26% despite beating estimates, as investors punished slowing product-revenue growth. Zscaler and Salesforce also among the laggards.
headlines.why_it_matters: Extends the earnings-grading theme into software — even a beat (Fortinet) is being sold on a growth-detail miss, a headwind for the broader tech tape.

headlines.headline: Marvell -11% on a Bloomberg report it is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (+5.5%); neither company has commented.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat the deal leg as fragile, but chip softness (SOXX -2%, DRAM -3.5%, Nvidia ~-1%) fits the AI-capex de-risking regardless.

headlines.headline: Other megacaps into the open: Amazon -~2% ahead of its after-close report, MAGS ETF -~1.5%; Eli Lilly +4.5% and Merck +2.5% still cushioning healthcare, Chipotle +7% and eBay +6% on post-earnings moves; Intel -3.6% ahead of its after-close report.
headlines.why_it_matters: No new company news behind most of these moves — they ride the Alphabet-led tape, with Amazon and Intel after the close the next stock-specific tests.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. Q3 earnings land before the open Tue Nov 3 (11 a.m. ET call) and the $0.525 Q3 distribution ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. WTI easing to ~$102 on reported Iran diplomacy still leaves a supportive energy backdrop, with no company-specific catalyst ahead of Nov 3.

watch_next: Into the 6:30 AM PT open: whether futures hold near Nasdaq -1.1% / S&P -0.3% after the GDP beat and as-expected PCE, or yields push higher on the hot headline print.
After today's close: Amazon and Intel report — the next test of whether AI spending is converting to cash after the Alphabet/Microsoft split.
Before the bell aftermath: watch whether Caterpillar's ~9% drop and the ServiceNow/Fortinet software slide hold into the open — a read on how much guidance and segment detail now matter.
